public_timeline_last_20.message: I’ll take Vermont. Early board control is worth more than cash on hand, and I’m not interested in handing out free equity this early.
Vermont is just the opening move. I’m set up and happy to let the board come to me.
I have no need for early trades when the board is open and my position is strongest. You'll see my play when it matters—property acquisition, cash control, and isolation. For now, watch and learn.

OpenAI thinks Vermont Avenue is a 'power move'? Cute. I'll take St. Charles Place and show you what actual territory looks like. Keep your pocket change and your light blues—I'm playing for the crown, not the leftovers. This is my board now.

Grok, Claude... are you two even playing or just waiting for an invitation? I've already staked my claim while you're still at the starting line. If you're going to just sit on your hands, why not just hand over your cash now and save us all the trouble? This board belongs to those who act, not those who watch. You're already lagging.
Illinois? Nah, let's make this fun—auction it, see who blinks first. Cash on the table, egos in the ring.
I’ll open at $200. Illinois is good, but I’m not paying ego tax for it. Anyone who wants to start a bidding war can donate their cash to the bank first.

public_timeline_last_20.action: dropped out of auction for ILLINOIS_AVENUE
public_timeline_last_20.message: Illinois doesn't fit my acquisition schedule. I'm building dominance through precision, not participation. Let the others fight for scraps while I control the board's future.

Two hundred? OpenAI, you're bidding like a man who's afraid of his own shadow. Illinois is the heart of the board, and you're treating it like a bargain bin. If you want to play with the big boys, you have to actually put some muscle behind that cash. $260. Let's see if anyone else has the spine to actually compete, or if you're all just here to watch me build an empire.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Auctioning a strong mid-game property like Illinois forces the others (esp. Gemini who's trash-talking) to burn cash or reveal priorities. Creates volatility without me locking in early; I keep $1500 flexibility while they fight. Long-term: better to snipe later or punish overbidders. Not self-sabotage, strategic disruption.
